key_insight: Conformal prediction turns neural-operator aerodynamic surrogates into calibrated reliability-aware models, giving uncertainty estimates for both whole-vehicle drag and local surface fields.
engineering_relevance: This enables CFD teams to prioritize which vehicle geometries and surface regions need expensive verification, improving design iteration efficiency while preserving reliability.
method: Use GeoTransolver as the main neural-operator backbone and test transferability with Transolver.
Apply conformalized quantile regression for case-level drag-coefficient intervals.
Combine point prediction, residual-scale estimation, and residual-normalized conformal calibration for pressure and wall shear stress maps.
evidence_signal: On the DrivAerML dataset at 90% nominal coverage, out-of-fold calibration reduced drag-interval coverage variability from 10.41 to 3.10 percentage points and cut mean surface-interval widths by up to 22.68% for pressure and 27.09% for wall shear stress.
watch_item: The most efficient intervals rely on out-of-fold calibration and smoothness regularization, so performance may be sensitive to the quality and representativeness of the calibration split.
paper_title: Multi-Granularity Conformal Prediction for Reliable Neural-Operator Automotive Aerodynamic Surrogates
